title: Storm declaration extended as claims hit 7500
full_text:
Storm declaration extended as claims hit 7500
The Insurance Council of Australia has extended its significant event declaration to include widespread storms that impacted Queensland and NSW yesterday.
Widespread thunderstorms struck from Coffs Harbour in NSW up to the Queensland border on Monday afternoon and overnight.
The declared insurance event now tracks claims from November 11-17, and insurers have received more than 7500 claims from severe weather over the period.
Food spoilage claims account for about 27% of home and contents claims after widespread power outages.
Monday's storms brought more strong winds, heavy rain and large hail, with damage including torn-off roofs, destroyed fences and water ingress.
In Queensland worst affected areas include Gatton, the Lockyer Valley, Logan and Woodford.
In NSW Wauchope, Lawrence, Mudgee, Singleton and South West Rocks on state's Mid North Coast are most impacted.
There were reports of hailstones up to 10 centimetres in diameter, and a possible tornado in South West Rocks. The Bureau of Meteorology is assessing radar imagery and reports.
"Communities across Queensland and NSW have now dealt with severe weather for a week, and yesterday's storms added to the damage. Extending the declaration means insurers can track the full impact of this event and keep resources where they're needed most," ICA CEO Andrew Hall said.
"Supporting recovery now matters, but so does investing in resilience so homes and businesses are better protected against the next storm."
Insurers have teams on the ground in both states to help policyholders, and the ICA is working with government and agencies.
